Rainfall and wave action will erode the steep banks of exposed soil causing increased turbidity. Presented as Exhibit 2 are excerpts from the Soil Conservation Service Soil Survey of Oconee County. South Carolina, which indicates that soils of the project area are extremely susceptible to erosion. This is equally true when upper horizon soils are stripped during borrow operations and the weathered parent material is exposed.
Staff concurs. See revised Section 2.1.3.
The high flows discharged to the Whitewater River arm during generation will create a highly mixed state in the area. Model studies and calculations of mixing numbers indicate that substantial decreases in the extent of the zone of mixing will be achieved by construction of a stone fill weir downstream of the discharge point. Nonquantitative model studies support the conclusion that mixed water flowing over this weir would not mix vertically with the lake main body but would seem to push the mixed water zone as a wedge or front displacing lake water before it. While this evidence would indicate definite improvements in lake conditions with the weir, no quantitative evidence is available to define the extent of this zone of influence over the lake.
